note: Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion `orb validate` (the Rust validator) reports for the same program, filtered to this rule's codes at program paths. The array/includes cases copy user_identity.rs tests array_includes_dynamic_object_get_haystack_is_not_checked, array_includes_list_call_haystack_checks_tail_only and array_includes_bare_literal_array_haystack_checks_every_element (run through a trait guard instead of calling check_comparison); the slot cases copy the_whole_user_in_a_required_emit_slot_is_an_error, the_whole_user_in_a_required_entity_field_is_an_error, a_presence_guard_or_a_default_clears_it (one case per clause) and a_user_field_read_is_not_the_whole_record, with their optional-slot controls. The rest pin branches those tests leave open: equality operators in guards and effects, the field as haystack, the expects shape as vocabulary (skipping imported bodies, and checked alongside a declared roster), sourceEntityDefinition provenance, page nav roles, the else branch of a presence if, and nested do blocks. The @user.<field> existence checks and the config-held role lists are not ported, so no case reads an undeclared @user field or compares a config role list.
